name: Status badges
summary: How to show the state of a domain object or a deadline with <aha-status-badge>: one box, four styles (quiet, emphasis, alert, plain), a dot only for published / live and closed, an icon or no marker for everything else, and when a badge is the wrong element.
highlights: One box, four styles, three markers
The dot is only for published / live and closed
Due states are badges too: alert, emphasis, plain
lead: A status badge tells the state of a domain object (a survey, a presentation, a course, a learner) or of a deadline in one glanceable, screen-reader-announced token. Every badge is the DS element <aha-status-badge>, so the box, the four styles and the markers stay the same in every app. This guideline says which style and marker a state takes, where the dot belongs, and what is not a badge at all.

skillRef.note: The DS owns this ruleset. The component contract (contracts/status-badge.json) carries the element API; this guideline carries the composition rules; the judge criteria and evals live in anti-slop/.

surfaceChoice.useFor: the lifecycle state of a survey, presentation or collector
surfaceChoice.example: Draft (pencil), Scheduled (calendar), Published (dot), Closed (dot), Archived (archive box)

surfaceChoice.useFor: how far a learner or a course has got
surfaceChoice.example: Not started (dashed circle), In progress (half-dashed circle), Completed (check circle)
5 days overdue (alert), Due today (emphasis + clock), Due in 9 days (plain), On time (plain + check), 4 days late (plain + late clock)

surfaceChoice.useFor: a state with no built-in status, or information that is not a status
surfaceChoice.example: Invited, Joined, 4/6, a slide type with its icon, Time out: quiet style

composedOf.use: the badge itself: <aha-status-badge> with status, look, marker and icon
the 16px icon marker, called by name from the registry through the badge's icon attribute
the quiet background; --aha-bg-container with --aha-border-strong (emphasis) or --aha-border-warning (alert) for the bordered styles
the alert warning icon, the only pink on any badge
the contrast target: a free-form label the user adds, removes or filters by is a Tag, not a status badge
the contrast target: a count bubble or notification dot on another element is a Badge, not a status badge

rules.rule: Render a status badge only for a value from a known status enum (lifecycle, progress, membership). A free-form label is a Tag; a count bubble or notification dot is a Badge.

Every badge is <aha-status-badge>. Set status for a built-in state, or look (quiet, emphasis, alert, plain) with an optional icon for a state the element does not know. Never hand-build the badge, restyle a Tag, or override the box (24px tall, 8px side padding, 6px radius, 14px semibold label, 6px gap).

A badge takes one of four styles: quiet (Gray 25, no border) for most states; emphasis (white, 1px grey inset border) for the live state and anything due now; alert (white, 1px black inset border, pink warning icon) for something the user must act on, such as overdue; plain (no box, Gray 80 regular text, optional icon) for information that needs no box. Pink appears only on the alert icon. No status gets a hue of its own: no green, red, amber or blue.

A badge has one marker before the label or none: a 16px icon from the DS icon registry, a 6px dot, or no marker. The built-in states carry theirs: Draft pencil, Scheduled calendar, Archived archive box, Not started dashed circle, In progress half-dashed circle, Completed check circle; Published, Live and Active a dark dot; Closed and Inactive a light dot. Never a dot and an icon together.

The dot is only for the published / live and closed lifecycle states (and active / inactive, which follow them). Every other state takes an icon or no marker. A dimension may mix dots and icons when each follows this rule (Draft with its pencil beside Published with its dot); a dot on any other state fails.

Information that is not a status but sits where badges sit (a counter such as 4/6, a slide or question type with its icon, Unanswered, Time out) uses look="quiet" (or plain), with or without an icon, never a dot. look="default" is a deprecated alias of quiet.

A due state is a badge in this family, set with look and icon rather than a status: overdue is alert; due today or due soon is emphasis with system-clock; due in N days is plain with no icon; on time is plain with system-check; N days late is plain with system-clock-late. The label carries the count from i18n.

An app that already owns an approved colour set for a result (Report: Correct, Partially correct, Incorrect) keeps those colours and takes only the box, through --aha-status-badge-bg and --aha-status-badge-fg set once in its stylesheet. Never use the two properties to tint a lifecycle, progress or due state, and never inline a hex on a badge.
The visible label is always sourced from i18n (t(`survey_status.${status}`) or the object's own namespace), in sentence case. Never hardcode the visible string.
Adding a state means adding a translation key AND choosing its style and marker in one mapping (one place per enum), so the same state never appears in two styles.
The element carries role="status" and an aria-label equal to the visible label (the DS element sets both). The text label is always present; a dot or an icon is decorative and never the only signal.
Existing screens on the aha-status-pill class convention keep working and are migrated to the element when they are next touched; new work never adds that markup.

reuseNote: Doc-only guideline. The component it describes ships as <aha-status-badge> (contracts/status-badge.json, lib/aha-status-badge.js) and is gated there.

selfCheck.label: every badge is <aha-status-badge> with a status or a look; the box is not overridden
the dot appears only on published / live / active and closed / inactive
counters, types, Unanswered and Time out use the quiet or plain style, never a dot
due states use alert, emphasis + clock or plain, from one mapping
no status has its own hue; pink only on the alert icon; no inline hex
label from i18n; role=status + aria-label match the visible text
